thread:
nate: Heads-up — we need a planned rolling cooldown + node reboots in the eu-central1 GPU pool tonight 22:00-01:00 UTC. Chiller vendor notified a controller firmware update and they want racks cooled down before swap.

sophia: Is this a full drain of the pool or per-rack? impact to Dedicated tenants? :warning:

nate: Per-rack, staggered. Expect ~10–15% throughput reduction for ~45m during the hottest phase if we don't backfill. For Dedicated customers on pinned capacity we'll maintain reserved nodes, but autoscaled workloads will feel it.

andrew: Can we backfill with spare capacity in us-west2 and route traffic across regions during the window? What's the cross-region egress cost look like?

nate: Yes — plan is to backfill with temporary burst nodes in us-west2 (quota and image already staged). Rough estimate: additional egress + instance costs ~ $2300/day if we fully backfill for peak traffic. Partial backfill halves that.

marco: Suggest staggering at rack-level with 5–7 minute gaps between cordons so the autoscaler has time to replenish. That keeps tail-latency SLOs less likely to breach.

jess: I'll coordinate customer comms. CS asks for 2-hour notice to affected tenants and a post-maint summary.

nate: Operator runbook (short):
```
# cordon + drain example (run per-node)
kubectl cordon gpu-node-123
kubectl drain gpu-node-123 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
# verify jobs moved and KV cache warmed on new nodes
```

andrew: Also add a preflight check 30m before start: confirm P95 latency < 150ms and KV cache hit-rate > 70%, otherwise abort/backoff.

marco: I'll prepare the orchestration script to apply `--max-surge=1` style pacing on the nodegroup and include a safety stop after 3 failures. Will post the gist in 10m. :gear:

nate: scheduling: proposed window tonight 22:00-01:00 UTC. Start with eu-central1-rack-A then B -> C. Total ~2.5h including verification and rollbacks.

sophia: SLA note — we should enable automatic fallback to previous model variant for latency-sensitive routes in case of cache warmup regressions. Add to rollout checklist.

jess: CS will send notice citing "planned infrastructure cooling maintenance" and the expected low-impact degradation window. I'll cc billing re: potential burst costs.

andrew: Oncall plan: nate leads, marco runs the orchestration, sophia monitors telemetry, jess handles comms. If any Dedicated tenant reports high errors, mark for immediate rollback and open support priority-1.

nate: drain-bot: create incident channel?

drain-bot: Created channel #inc-1769804321-cooldown. Auto-posts: preflight checklist 30m, start marker, per-rack completion, post-checks.

marco: Linked the orchestration script: https://gist.gith.fake/abcd1234 (will update with real link). Includes stagger timings, retry backoff, and a dry-run mode.

jess: CS draft sent to internal review. We'll delay external notice to 2h prior, unless the preflight reveals risk and we postpone. :thumbsup:

sophia: Also add a quick billing estimate to the ticket so finance sees the potential $ impact.

nate: OK locking this in unless objections. Final reminder: runbook owner is marco, rollback owner is andrew. Ping me immediately for SLO regressions.

marco: no objections, prepping dry-run in staging now.

andrew: I'll watch for autoscaler thrash and set a temporary higher min-nodes threshold +10% before draining.

jess: Noted. I'll be on standby at start time for external comms.

nate: Thanks team — will post the formal calendar invite and update the maintenance board. :white_check_mark:
